newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea business group sees slow recovery in Q3.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea business group sees slow recovery in Q3.

text.p: South Korean businesses expect a sluggish economic recovery in the third quarter of 1997 despite some improvement in major industrial sectors, a corporate survey by the Korea Chamber of Commerce said on Tuesday.
The Business Survey Index (BSI), provided by the chamber, stood at 92 for the third quarter, against 76 for the second quarter and 58 for the first.
A BSI figure higher than 100 means the business outlook is bullish. Anything less than 100 means the outlook is bearish.
The group said domestic consumption and corporate liquidity conditions would remain troubled with the BSI at 90 and 69 respectively for the third quarter.
However, exports were expected to improve in the third quarter with a BSI standing at 103, it said.
The group said an increase in new orders for the shipbuilding industry and rising auto exports on the yen's strength against the dollar were likely to lead the recovery.
The electronic parts and telecommunications businesses were also forecast to pick up thanks to rising exports of telecommunications equipment and higher prices for semiconductors.
But the survey showed a slump would continue in the metals and machinery sectors.
The survey, which covered 1,993 companies, had a response rate of 89.7 percent.
